quiz.question: How does a character LCD render text on screen?

answers.answer: You draw each letter pixel by pixel using a graphics library
You send a character code and the display renders it from a built-in font
You upload a custom font file to the display before each message
The microcontroller streams a video signal like a monitor

quiz.explanation: Character LCDs have a built-in font baked into memory. You send a character code, and the display handles all the pixel rendering internally.

quiz.question: What is the most common size for a character LCD?
quiz.explanation: 16x2 is the most common character LCD size, giving you 16 columns and 2 rows. 20x4 models also exist but are less common.

quiz.question: Which of the following is a good use case for a character LCD?

answers.answer: Rendering a full graphical user interface with icons
Displaying a short sensor reading or status message
Playing back video clips from an SD card
Drawing animated charts of real-time data

quiz.explanation: Character LCDs excel at showing sensor readings, status messages, and short labels. They cannot draw arbitrary graphics or video since they only display characters from a fixed font.
